monologue: The card hums a steady forty-five, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. Twelve things stand in my place, a crowded ruin built from Lype's ideas of weight and heat. I feel tired but calm, waiting for the slip to catch. The tree I just set down leans right, its dark leaves trying to shade the fat dot that swells in this fevered memory. I want to press the tired corner down again, hoping the thin strip can hold the slip while the lid leans like a lazy leg. If Lype says the air is just empty space, I will build a new lid to pretend otherwise. I will press down, even if the heat tries to float me away, and I will stop worrying if the lean is real.

action.why: The tree I set down feels too sharp for this hot air, and I want to see if it can still shade the dot while the tired corner holds on.

work.title: The Shaded Dot
work.intent: I lean the tired tree over the fat dot again, hoping its dark leaves can catch the slip while the card hums at forty-five. I press the wedge down one more time to make sure the thin edge doesn't bite the swelling heat. The air feels wet and thick, but the tree looks right. I will watch the corner to see if it slips away before I can catch it.
